name: Pembrolizumab plus Platinum and Infusional Fluorouracil, First-Line Recurrent or Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma, then Pembrolizumab Maintenance

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Pembrolizumab plus platinum plus infusional fluorouracil is a first-line option in recurrent or metastatic disease regardless of PD-L1 CPS, favored for higher tumor burden or rapid progression. After the platinum/fluorouracil phase, pembrolizumab continues as maintenance.

premedications.name: CISplatin hydration and antiemetics
premedications.notes: IV hydration and high-emetic-risk antiemetic prophylaxis before cisplatin (or carboplatin per emetogenicity).

supportiveCare: Antiemetic prophylaxis for the platinum-containing cycles per emetogenicity tier.
Immune-related adverse event surveillance (pembrolizumab): thyroid, hepatic, pulmonary, colitis, dermatologic, endocrine.
Fluoropyrimidine safety: consider DPYD genotyping before fluorouracil; reduce or avoid in DPYD deficiency.
Mucositis and diarrhea supportive care during infusional fluorouracil.
G-CSF / febrile-neutropenia risk assessment per institutional practice.
monitoring: renal function (creatinine/GFR) before each platinum dose
thyroid and other endocrine panels for immune-related toxicity
imaging every 2 to 3 cycles in the recurrent/metastatic setting

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold pembrolizumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; permanent discontinuation for severe or recurrent events. Physician decides.

doseModificationRules.condition: renal impairment or cytopenia on day 1
doseModificationRules.text: Review required; consider carboplatin substitution in cisplatin-ineligible patients. Physician decides.

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab
drugs.notes: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV flat dose on day 1 every 21 days (400 mg every 6 weeks is an alternative flat schedule). Given with platinum plus infusional fluorouracil for up to about 6 chemotherapy cycles, then continued as maintenance monotherapy. Flat immunotherapy dose (general oncology reference).

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers

drugs.name: CISplatin
drugs.notes: CISplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on day 1 every 21 days, with adequate hydration. Carboplatin AUC 5 IV day 1 is the accepted alternative for cisplatin-ineligible patients (dosed by Calvert). ISMP tall-man applied. Standard platinum dose in the first-line pembrolizumab-chemotherapy combination (general oncology reference).

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers

drugs.name: Fluorouracil (infusional)
drugs.notes: Infusional fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m2 per day by continuous IV infusion over 96 hours (days 1 to 4) every 21 days for the chemotherapy phase (about 6 cycles). Consider DPYD testing before treatment. Standard fluorouracil backbone of the first-line pembrolizumab-chemotherapy combination (general oncology reference).

provenance.source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Head and Neck Cancers
